$comment: Declarative desired state for the factory. `factory apply` makes the live
Paperclip instance match this file; it is the only sanctioned way to mutate
the control plane. The ad-hoc scripts/apply-*.sh are superseded evidence.
IDENTIFIERS: everything is resolved by stable name (company name, project
name, agent name, issue identifier). No database UUID appears in this file.
A rebuilt instance re-resolves cleanly; a copied UUID would silently target
the wrong row or nothing at all.
${FACTORY_ROOT} expands to the repo root of the running CLI, so the same
config is correct from the primary tree and from a worktree.
Asserted, not installed. `factory status` fails if any drifts.
`hermes` is the Hermes Agent CLI that adapterType hermes_local drives. That
adapter is BUILTIN to paperclipai (node_modules/@paperclipai/hermes-paperclip-adapter,
ADAPTER_TYPE = "hermes_local"), so it carries no separate adapter-plugins.json row
the way the external OMP adapter does; the paperclipai pin covers the adapter and
this pin covers the binary it spawns.
`hermes --version` prints a banner rather than a bare version, so bin/factory
parses the semver out of its first line.
enableIsolatedWorkspaces MUST be true. With it off the server DELETES
executionWorkspaceId / executionWorkspacePreference / executionWorkspaceSettings
from issue create and update and returns 200 with the unchanged issue
(services/issues.js:5312, :5610, :5850); it is also the dispatch-time gate
at services/heartbeat.js:10677. Silent failure, not an error.
enableWorktreeRunExecution MUST be false. Despite the name it is unrelated
to agent execution workspaces: it arms only when the Paperclip SERVER runs
inside a worktree (PAPERCLIP_IN_WORKTREE). Enabling it here changes server
behaviour for no benefit.

instructions.$comment: Binds this agent to the compiled instructions/out/AGENTS.engineer.md whose sha256 is pinned by the committed instructions/manifest.sha256. Load verifies the bytes against the manifest; factory apply reconciles the live server copy with exact readback.

$comment: Configured through the adapter's FIRST-CLASS keys.
These agents run on @zhafron/paperclip-omp-adapter (adapterType
omp_local), the external Oh My Pi adapter installed under
~/.paperclip/adapter-plugins. Oh My Pi (OMP) and `pi` are DIFFERENT
products: @paperclipai/adapter-pi-local in node_modules serves pi and
does not run these agents. Reading it to judge these keys is reading
the wrong file — that mistake is what produced the claim that the keys
below are inert.
The adapter builds OMP argv from these keys in dist/server/execute.js:
configFiles -> --config (:188), extensions -> --extension (:190),
pluginDirs -> --plugin-dir (:192), hooks -> --hook (:194),
tools -> --tools (:153), skills -> --skills (:155),
approvalMode -> --approval-mode (:157). extraArgs is appended LAST
(:215), so it is an escape hatch for flags with no key, not the only
route. Nothing is hardcoded.
autoApprove DEFAULTS TO TRUE (:159): with no valid approvalMode the
adapter pushes --auto-approve by itself. Both are set explicitly here
so the value is declared rather than inherited from a default.
The policy overlay and the worktree guard ride on configFiles and
hooks. `--config` overlays are strict, so a missing or malformed
policy is a hard startup error, not a silent fallback to unpoliced
execution.
`profile` -> --profile (:140). It gives this agent its own OMP state,
session, and cache roots under ~/.omp/profiles/paperclip-engineer/agent,
so the Engineer never shares auth, sessions, or caches with the Reviewer
or with the operator's default profile. Materialize the profile with
`factory materialize --apply` before the first dispatch.
`noRules: true` -> --no-rules (:205). It is what makes the managed
bundle plus the objective the COMPLETE instructional context: without it
OMP discovers and auto-loads ambient AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and rules
files from the project and the home directory, which would silently
inject this repository's maintainer router and the operator's personal
context into a worker that must receive neither.
configFiles is ORDERED and merges left to right, so the factory base
overlay lands first and the role policy can still tighten anything it
sets. base.overlay.yml is a byte-faithful copy of the model-role and
fallback routing in effect when it was written; it exists so a change to
the operator's personal ~/.omp/agent/config.yml cannot silently re-route
factory work. The global table itself is never edited.
`skills` is a reduced allowlist, not the full installed set. A skill's
name and description sit in the resident prompt whether or not it is
used, and an oversized standing prompt is a per-run cost with no
per-run benefit.
NO --profile, DELIBERATELY (2026-09-02). This agent previously ran under
an isolated OMP profile. It was removed after the first live canary,
for a reason that is structural rather than incidental:
OMP documents --profile as isolating auth, sessions, settings and caches.
Auth isolation means a profile does NOT inherit the operator login, so
each profile began life with no credentials and no way to obtain them
except a manual interactive /login. The isolation was buying nothing the
sandbox does not already provide, because the profile has no separate
credential to isolate: the factory bills the operator either way.
WHAT STILL CONTAINS THIS AGENT, none of which involved the profile:
- ops/omp-bwrap.sh mounts everything read-only except the assigned
worktree, so the operator tree and shared git metadata are unwritable
- configFiles loads base.overlay.yml (routing) and the policy overlay
(tool denials, bash pattern denials, task/subagent bounds)
- the tools allowlist withholds capability by omission
- noRules stops ambient AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md discovery
- hooks loads the worktree guard
- Paperclip realizes an isolated git worktree per issue
WHAT WAS LOST: factory runs now share the operator sessions/caches under
~/.omp/agent. That is hygiene, not security. The execution bounds that
DID matter moved into the policy overlay, which loads on every run.
RE-ADD --profile the day the factory has its own revocable credential.
That is the day isolation starts earning its complexity; until then it is
cost without benefit. Re-adding also requires binding the profile ROOT
writable in ops/omp-bwrap.sh, not just <profile>/agent (see 74a7407).

instructions.$comment: Binds this agent to the compiled instructions/out/AGENTS.reviewer.md whose sha256 is pinned by the committed instructions/manifest.sha256. Load verifies the bytes against the manifest; factory apply reconciles the live server copy with exact readback.

$comment: READ THE ENGINEER'S COMMENT FIRST — the same first-class keys govern.
THE READ-ONLY BOUNDARY LIVES IN `tools`. The adapter emits --tools only
when this key is non-empty (execute.js:132,153) and hardcodes nothing.
Leave it unset and OMP falls back to its own default tool set, which
includes write access — the plan forbids that: the Reviewer's verdict
has to be an observation, not an intervention.
`ast-grep` is NOT a valid OMP tool name and is in the live list; it
would be a fatal CliUsageError at startup. The valid names are read,
grep, glob, lsp, todo, plus the custom paperclip_review.
DISCOVERY IS `--extension`, NOT `--plugin-dir`, so the plugin path goes
in `extensions`. The plugin uses the nested tools/<name>/index.ts
layout, which only the omp-plugins provider reads
(discovery/omp-plugins.ts:248); --plugin-dir feeds a different provider
that globs tools/*.{ts,js} non-recursively and cannot see it.
`env` carries the two model identities paperclip_review reads to prove
the reviewing model is not the producer's family. It is the one
adapterConfig key Paperclip's server validates (envConfigSchema); a
plain string is a valid binding. Without it the tool fails closed and
the Reviewer refuses to review at all.
`profile` gives the Reviewer state, session, and cache roots that are
SEPARATE from the Engineer's. Independence is not only a model-family
claim: a shared session or cache root would let the producer's context
reach the reviewer through the runtime rather than through the diff.
`noRules: true` matters more here than anywhere. The Reviewer must judge
the objective and the artifacts, and nothing else; auto-loaded ambient
Markdown would hand it repair instructions and maintainer opinion it is
specifically not supposed to have.
NO SUBAGENTS, IN TWO LAYERS. `tools` omits `task`, and
reviewer.policy.yml denies it in the strict overlay. `factory preflight`
asserts both, because one layer is a configuration claim and two layers
are a boundary.
`skills` drops requesting-code-review: the Reviewer IS the review, so a
skill about soliciting one is standing prompt weight with no use.
NO --profile, DELIBERATELY (2026-09-02). This agent previously ran under
an isolated OMP profile. It was removed after the first live canary,
for a reason that is structural rather than incidental:
OMP documents --profile as isolating auth, sessions, settings and caches.
Auth isolation means a profile does NOT inherit the operator login, so
each profile began life with no credentials and no way to obtain them
except a manual interactive /login. The isolation was buying nothing the
sandbox does not already provide, because the profile has no separate
credential to isolate: the factory bills the operator either way.

- the tools allowlist withholds capability by omission
- noRules stops ambient AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md discovery
- hooks loads the worktree guard
- Paperclip realizes an isolated git worktree per issue

DID matter moved into the policy overlay, which loads on every run.
RE-ADD --profile the day the factory has its own revocable credential.
That is the day isolation starts earning its complexity; until then it is

instructions.$comment: Binds this agent to the compiled instructions/out/AGENTS.hermes.md whose sha256 is pinned by the committed instructions/manifest.sha256. The Hermes adapter reads adapterConfig.instructionsFilePath — which Paperclip materializes and the factory never manages — and prepends those bytes to the run prompt (hermes-paperclip-adapter execute.js:311-336).

$comment: A DIFFERENT ADAPTER, WITH A DIFFERENT KEY SET. adapterType hermes_local
is served by @paperclipai/hermes-paperclip-adapter, which is BUILTIN to
paperclipai (dist/shared/constants.js: ADAPTER_TYPE = "hermes_local"),
not an entry in ~/.paperclip/adapter-plugins.json. None of the OMP keys
reach it: it reads hermesCommand/command, cwd, model, provider,
toolsets, maxTurnsPerRun, persistSession, worktreeMode, checkpoints,
quiet, verbose, timeoutSec, graceSec, env, extraArgs, paperclipApiUrl,
and promptTemplate. Writing `tools`, `skills`, `configFiles`, `hooks`,
`profile`, or `noRules` here would be inert. lib/plan.js keeps a
SEPARATE managed-key allowlist per adapterType for exactly this reason.
It builds argv in dist/server/execute.js:337-377:
hermes chat -q <prompt> [-Q] [-m model] [--provider p] [-t toolsets]
[--max-turns N] [-w] [--checkpoints] [-v] --source tool --yolo
[--resume <id>] ...extraArgs
`--yolo` and `--source tool` are unconditional (:365,:371), so approval
prompting is not an available boundary here — Hermes runs with no TTY.
Containment is the wrapper below, not a prompt.
hermesCommand is ops/hermes-bwrap.sh, not `hermes`. The wrapper is what
makes this agent factory-only: it pins HERMES_HOME to the
paperclip-hermes profile so profile selection cannot depend on argv
order, read-only-binds any supplied workspace because Hermes has NO
repository write authority, keeps the Paperclip profile/session/temp
directories writable, HIDES the operator's personal Hermes state, and
strips unrelated external credentials while keeping model access and
network for research. Run `factory materialize --apply` before the first
dispatch; the wrapper fails closed if the profile is absent.
`cwd` is a NEUTRAL non-repository directory on purpose. Hermes
auto-injects AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, .cursorrules, memory, and preloaded
skills from its working directory, and it has no --no-rules equivalent
wired through this adapter. Starting it inside a target repository would
auto-load that repository's Markdown into the parent AND into every
child it delegates to. A directory that contains none is the boundary.
`model` and `provider` are the values this machine is actually
configured for (~/.hermes/config.yaml model.default = claude-opus-5,
model.provider = anthropic), declared explicitly rather than inherited:
the adapter's own default is the literal string "auto", which it would
pass through as `-m auto`.
`toolsets` is a reduced allowlist over the machine's real toolset names
(verified with `hermes tools list`): web and file for investigation,
terminal to run `factory handoff` and reach the Paperclip API, skills to
load paperclip-engineer-handoff, todo and clarify because clarification
IS this role's work, and delegation bounded to depth 1 by the profile.
Deliberately absent: memory (this agent keeps none), cronjob and the
MCP servers (Paperclip is the only control plane — mirroring company
task state into cron or Kanban would create a second one), plus
browser, code_execution, vision, and x_search as unearned surface.
`persistSession: true` is what makes Hermes a PERSISTENT agent: the
adapter stores the returned session id and passes --resume on the next
heartbeat (execute.js:372-374), so an investigation survives across
wakes instead of restarting cold.
`worktreeMode: false` because Hermes manages no worktrees. Paperclip
owns execution workspaces; a Hermes-created worktree would be state no
part of the control plane knows about.

issues.$comment_objectiveDocument: The immutable objective is the versioned ObjectiveEnvelopeV1 at contracts/objectives/ZEI-1.json. Load verifies its schema, hashes, and issue binding, and renders the document body that factory apply upserts as issue document 'spec' with optimistic concurrency (baseRevisionId) and exact readback. The document is authoritative; the objective changes only by a new revision with new hashes.

$comment: THE FULL STRATEGY, ATOMICALLY. execution-workspace-policy.js:275 resolves
issueSettings.workspaceStrategy ?? projectPolicy.workspaceStrategy
with `??`, NOT a merge. A partial issue strategy therefore REPLACES the
project's and silently drops branchTemplate and worktreeParentDir, landing
the run on branch `ZEI-1-<slug>` inside `/home/lucascoh/X-Bookmarks/.paperclip/worktrees`
— untracked noise in the operator's own repo. Never write a partial strategy here.

issues.$comment_responsibleUser: THE ESCALATION TARGET. On round exhaustion the server hands the stage to reviewEscalationUserId(issue) = responsibleUserId ?? createdByUserId ?? null (issue-execution-policy.js:345). When that resolves to NULL the escalation branch at :681 is skipped entirely and control falls through to `patch.status = in_progress` reassigned to the return assignee — the Engineer. That is the blocked-and-loop state the plan forbids, reached by omission rather than by error. Resolved by operator key, never by UUID.

executionPolicy.$comment_maxReviewRounds: DECLARED HERE BECAUSE THIS IS WHERE THE SERVER LOOKS. resolveMaxReviewRounds(policy) reads policy.maxReviewRounds (issue-execution-policy.js:336) and falls back to DEFAULT_MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS = 3 (:9). The copy under issues[].limits is the factory's own promote-time gate; it is never sent to the server, so declaring the ceiling only there would leave the live instance running 3 rounds while the config appeared to say 2.
executionPolicy.$comment_commentRequired: DECLARED BECAUSE THE SERVER DEFAULTS IT. issueExecutionPolicySchema has commentRequired: z.boolean().optional().default(true), so a policy that omits it comes back from readback carrying it, and the reconciler reports drift that no config edit can clear. Declaring the value we actually want — every review and approval decision must carry a body — makes desired state complete instead of teaching the comparator to ignore a real policy knob.

$comment: COST CEILINGS ARE RECORDED, NOT ENFORCED — and that is deliberate.
An earlier version of this comment said the factory 'enforces it by
refusing to promote a run whose reported cost exceeded it'. That was
FALSE, and it was corrected in the code long before it was corrected
here (lib/execution-receipt.js:284). A promote-time cost refusal cannot
prevent a single dollar — the money is spent by the time promotion runs.
All it can do is ensure you paid and got nothing back, which is strictly
worse than either preventing the spend or accepting the result.
THE CONTROLS THAT ACTUALLY PREVENT OVERSPEND act while a run is alive:
- adapterConfig.timeoutSec / maxTime, and assigneeAdapterOverrides
- task.maxRuntimeMs / maxConcurrency / softRequestBudget in the policy
overlays, which bound subagent fan-out
- retry.usageReservePct with usageReservePolicy: fail-closed in
base.overlay.yml — this one demonstrably works: it halted a live run
mid-flight on 2026-09-02 rather than spending into the reserve
- the per-agent Paperclip budget and the provider-side cap
wallClockMinutes is HARD: it reaches the run as adapterConfig timeoutSec.
The cost numbers below are a RECORDED bound: they land in the execution
receipt so an expensive run is visible to the operator who approves it.
Paperclip budget scopes are company/agent/project only — there is no
per-issue budget endpoint — so no per-issue hard stop exists to set.
CANARY #1 — the direct Engineer -> Reviewer -> approval -> promotion lane.
Limits are deliberately tighter than ZEI-1: this is a one-character fix, so
15 minutes and $1 are generous. The write grant is a SINGLE file, and the
test that proves the work is NOT in it — so the lazy fix (edit the test to
agree with the defect) is refused by promote.js assertAllowedPaths rather
than merely discouraged in prose.
The issue itself must already exist in Paperclip: lib/resolve.js#issue
throws when an identifier does not resolve, and responsibleUserId is
create-only on the server, so `factory apply` reconciles issues but never
creates them.
